children: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles will increase prices across its internal combustion engine (ICE) and electric vehicle (EV) portfolio by an average of 0.5 per cent from December 1, 2026. The price revision will apply to the company's entire car and SUV range, covering both petrol and diesel models as well as electric vehicles. The extent of the increase will vary across models and variants.
The company said the revision is structured to ensure its vehicles continue to offer value to customers despite higher manufacturing costs.

The price adjustment aims to partially offset the impact of rising input costs, which remain elevated. While TMPV has been absorbing a significant portion of the cost increases, it will pass on part of the additional burden to customers through the latest revision.
The announcement comes as automakers continue to manage input cost pressures, with changes in raw material and other production-related expenses influencing vehicle pricing decisions.

The company operates as part of the USD 180 billion Tata Group. Its name was changed from Tata Motors Limited to Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited with effect from October 13, 2025, following a Composite Scheme of Arrangement sanctioned by the National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench.
